definition: Anemia is a condition where hemoglobin levels in the blood are lower than the typical adult reference range. In many adults, hemoglobin is usually between approximately 12–16 g/dL, although ranges may vary by laboratory and individual factors.
Hemoglobin is a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout the body. It is measured in grams per deciliter (g/dL) in blood tests.
Iron supplements are medications commonly prescribed to support hemoglobin production when iron deficiency is suspected or confirmed.
A follow-up appointment is typically scheduled to monitor progress, review laboratory results, or assess response to treatment.
